newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu recuperates in lavish French Riviera villa.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu recuperates in lavish French Riviera villa.

text.p: An eery quiet reigned outside the lavish pink and white marble villa on the French Riviera where Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko rested up on Tuesday while his country edged toward disaster.

Mobutu, who has been in Lausanne where he underwent surgery for prostate cancer in August, has remained silent and out of sight since fighting broke out in his country between Zairean troops and Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels, trapping more than one million starving refugees who hover on the brink of catastrophe.
A crowd of television cameramen and photographers strained in vain for a glimpse of the ailing leader who arrived from Lausanne with his 20-member entourage aboard DC-8 airliner on Monday.
There was no sign of life from inside the vast, three-story Victorian house, flanked by sunflowers, gladiolas and gerberas.
Perched on the edge of this tiny cape between Menton and Monaco and overlooking the Mediterranean, the Villa del Mare was bought from Saudi billionaire Akrem Ojjeh in 1986 for an undisclosed sum.
Eucalyptus, bamboo and palm trees dot the rolling 10 hectares (25 acres) of grounds which slowly descend to the sea, offering a view of nearby Monaco.
The property includes three buildings to house staff who enter the estate by a rear gate.
French policemen patrol the perimetre of the grounds, more worried about sheltering reporters from Mobutu's body guards than protecting the African president from danger.
On Monday guards equipped with pistols confiscated the camera of a French television crew and threatened to break the legs of any journalist who came too near the gate.
Mobutu's spokesman in Kinshasa said the leader would be in France for just a few days before returning home.
"The treatment he was undergoing ended on October 30 and no other medical test is scheduled," the spokesman said.
United Nations envoy Raymond Chretien was due to arrive later on Tuesday to discuss the chaos in Zaire ahead of an emergency meeting of the U.N. Security Council.

France has proposed sending a multinational force to open safe corridors to ensure that food and medical aid reach the refugees, some of whom are said to have been without water or food for up to two weeks.
